title: From the Editor — The Farther Rider
settingText: The Long Mile under a huge bleached sky. A white ridge cuts across the upper distance. A single tiny rider-like silhouette stands far away, unreadable and completely non-glowing. Enormous negative space and honest frontier realism.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 8. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Distance is supposed to be one of the honest things.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A mile is a mile.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A ridge is where you left it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Walk toward something and, eventually, it gets closer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Sunfields have been strange in ways people can explain: bad memory, good gossip, grief, manipulation, coincidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Those explanations have carried the story a long way.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: On the Long Mile, there is a rider on a white ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nobody knows who he is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For now, that is not the unsettling part.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: Same Road
summary: Raina and Samuel catch the trio after Rowan Hold and ask to travel on the same road rather than operating ahead and behind. The arrangement is practical, uneasy and explicitly temporary.

panelPlan.text: Wide Long Mile: the rig moves through pale open terrain while two figures approach from a rear trail.
Raina and Samuel catch up on foot and mount, dusty enough to look like travelers rather than pursuers.
Their bedrolls remain separate from the rig while they talk, visually preserving the provisional relationship.
Brandon lets Jessie decide because it is her vehicle and her fuel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I want to stop working ahead of you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You already stopped being allowed to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Then let us travel where you can see us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That would simplify several conversations.

title: Jessie's Terms
summary: Jessie sets the conditions: no disappearing ahead, no planted stories, no private messages to settlements. Raina and Samuel accept because the old method has already failed as an explanation.

panelPlan.text: The group walks beside the rig while Jessie lists conditions without stopping the day's travel.
Raina closes the notebook she once used to plan encounters and puts it away.
Samuel agrees not to initiate conversations about Brandon with communities they have not yet reached.
Eva points out that ordinary conversation will still spread their presence once people see them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: No going ahead. No notes left for towns. No helpful strangers prepared for us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I won't go ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I won't plant another identity.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: People can still gossip after we arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: People are allowed to be people. You two are done engineering them.

title: The Rider on the Ridge
summary: During the travel negotiation, Eva notices a solitary mounted silhouette on a pale southern ridge. Nothing about the figure is visibly supernatural or threatening.

panelPlan.text: The conversation continues while a tiny rider silhouette becomes visible high on a white ridge far to the south.
Eva is the first to notice because she is scanning the horizon while others watch one another.
Raina uses brass optics but cannot resolve face, clothing detail or mount beyond an ordinary rider-like shape.
Brandon looks once and returns attention to the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: There's a rider on the south ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: How far?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: About a mile.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Less than that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Coming toward us?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They're holding position.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then let them have the ridge.

title: How Far
summary: Eva and Raina disagree about the Rider's distance because the open terrain gives unusually clear landmarks. They decide to measure by walking the road rather than chasing off-route.

panelPlan.text: Raina identifies a split white stone below the ridge and a dark notch beyond it as fixed reference points.
Eva estimates the ridge at one mile; Raina estimates closer to three quarters.
They mark their current position with a cairn at the road edge.
The group continues on its normal route, which angles naturally toward the southern terrain for the next stretch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We don't have to chase them. The road is already taking us closer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Then we can test the distance without changing course.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You made that sound less exciting than it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That is intentional.

title: The Dry Wash
summary: After crossing a dry wash that should have reduced the distance substantially, the Rider still appears nearly unchanged against the same ridge notch.

panelPlan.text: Eva and Raina descend into a shallow dry wash while Jessie and Samuel guide the rig through the easier crossing.
The ridge disappears briefly behind the wash wall.
When they climb out, the same silhouette appears against the same notch with nearly the same apparent scale.
Eva looks back at the distant cairn and realizes how much ground they actually covered.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We should be closer by now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Close enough that I shouldn't still be estimating the same distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Heat can lie to your eyes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: It can. Keep that explanation alive.

title: Landmarks
summary: The terrain itself appears trustworthy: foreground stones and ridge features shift exactly as expected while only the Rider's apparent distance resists easy interpretation.

panelPlan.text: Brandon joins Eva and Raina near a distinctive split stone visible from the earlier marker.
They compare the stone's changed angle and the ridge notch's larger scale, confirming real forward movement.
The Rider remains a small silhouette farther up the same visual line.
Brandon suggests the figure may have moved while hidden by terrain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: We lost sight of them in the wash.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Long enough to move backward?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Long enough to move somewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That is still better than assuming distance changed.

title: One Ridge
summary: Eva asks to take the natural cut to the ridge because they are close enough that reaching the landmark would settle whether the figure has simply been moving.

panelPlan.text: The road divides around a low rise. Jessie identifies a southern cut that rejoins the main route later and passes near the ridge.
Eva argues they can investigate without sacrificing the day's destination.
Samuel prefers the main road but does not try to overrule the group.
Brandon agrees to the southern cut only because it is still a legitimate route, not a chase across open ground.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The south cut reaches that ridge and joins the road again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It costs an hour if the ground is decent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: One ridge. Then we go back to traveling somewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I would prefer somewhere.

title: The Ridge They Saw
summary: The group reaches the physical ridge they had been using as the Rider's position. The distinctive split stone and notch confirm it is the same landform.

panelPlan.text: Jessie points out the split stone now at arm's reach and the exact notch overhead.
Brandon scratches a small temporary mark in loose dust beside the stone rather than on the rock itself.
The crest ahead is empty.
Eva climbs the last few yards expecting tracks or a rider beyond the top.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: This is the ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then they moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Let's see whether the ground agrees.

title: No Tracks
summary: The ridge crest shows no obvious recent hoofprints or passage, but hard wind-scoured ground prevents that absence from becoming proof of anything impossible.

panelPlan.text: Raina kneels at the crest, examining hard pale ground broken by stone and wind-scoured patches.
Eva looks for a line of prints down either side and finds none.
Brandon points out several places where even their own footsteps barely register.
Raina records 'no visible tracks' rather than 'no tracks.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nothing came down this side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Nothing left a mark we can see.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Those are not the same claim.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I know. I dislike the careful version.

title: The Farther Ridge
summary: Across the next basin, a rider silhouette stands on a farther ridge. The figure is visually similar but too distant to prove it is the same person.

panelPlan.text: Eva reaches the crest and looks across the next shallow basin.
On a farther ridge, another unreadable rider silhouette stands against the sky.
The whole group gathers without rushing forward.
Composition must preserve the possibility of a second ordinary rider; no visual duplication effect or supernatural cue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Could be another rider.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Could be.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Two people can own the same kind of hat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You don't sound convinced.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't sound decided.

title: Bad Explanations
summary: The group inventories ordinary explanations without choosing among them: mirage, second rider, hidden route, bad distance judgment and deliberate evasion.

panelPlan.text: They shelter briefly in the lee of the ridge while the distant silhouette remains visible.
Eva lists possibilities. Raina rejects only claims that contradict observed facts, not possibilities she finds unlikely.
Jessie notes that heat shimmer can distort size and position without making geography impossible.
Brandon eats while they theorize, refusing to elevate the stranger above the rest of the day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Mirage. Second rider. Hidden trail. We judged the distance badly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Heat can move an image without moving the person.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: None of those explanations fits every observation yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then don't marry one.

title: Back to the Road
summary: Eva wants one more ridge. Brandon refuses to spend the day pursuing a stranger who has not approached, threatened or asked anything of them.

panelPlan.text: The southern cut descends back toward the main road while the farther ridge remains in view.
Eva argues that one more approach could distinguish a second rider from impossible distance.
Brandon points out that curiosity is not automatically permission to pursue somebody across open country.
Samuel unexpectedly agrees with Brandon, having recently learned what investigation can do to people treated as material.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: One more ridge would tell us more.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It might tell us the stranger wanted to be left alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We finally have something that does not fit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That does not make the person ours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: He is right about that part.

title: Evening Camp
summary: Hours later, the group makes camp along its original route with the southern ridges behind them. The day returns to ordinary concerns long enough for the Rider to become background rather than pursuit.

panelPlan.text: Late light over a small roadside camp: bedrolls, cooking pot, rig checks and tired bodies.
Brandon repairs a strap. Jessie checks a wheel hub. Samuel cooks something unambitious.
Eva and Raina compare their notes but do not leave camp to investigate.
The southern ridge line is behind them and partly obscured by terrain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I still think we should have tried another approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow's position may tell us more than chasing tonight would.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That sounds like patience.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Do not make it ceremonial.

title: Closer
summary: Near sunset, Jessie looks up and sees a rider silhouette on a low rise only a few hundred yards from camp. The figure remains motionless and unreadable.

panelPlan.text: Jessie looks past Brandon while reaching for a tool and stops.
On a low rise north of the southern ridges, a rider silhouette stands much closer than the earlier figure.
The group does not draw weapons or surround the camp; the figure has made no threatening move.
Eva turns slowly to confirm what Jessie saw.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Don't turn around quickly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You know that makes everybody turn around.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is a lot closer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: It is.

title: Raina Recognizes the Pattern
summary: Raina's reaction is more unsettling than the Rider itself. Samuel recognizes that she has seen the same relationship between pursuit and distance before.

panelPlan.text: Raina stares at the closer figure with none of her usual eagerness to measure or approach.
Samuel watches Raina rather than the Rider and remembers a cryptic entry from her old notes.
He asks about Red Wash, a place Eva and Jessie have never heard mentioned.
Raina closes her optics instead of lifting them again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: This is what happened at Red Wash.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What happened at Red Wash?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I saw a rider I could not get closer to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: When?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Months before I met Samuel.

title: Red Wash
summary: Raina recounts the earlier sighting carefully. She was following an unrelated lead near Red Wash, rode toward a distant rider for hours and ended with a lathered horse while the figure appeared farther away.

panelPlan.text: The current Rider remains visible on the low rise while Raina speaks, making the account feel observational rather than a flashback spectacle.
Raina says she first assumed a navigation error, then a mirage, then deliberate evasion.
She changed angles twice and used fixed rocks for bearings, but never reached the figure.
She stopped because her horse was exhausted, not because she found an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I rode toward it until my horse was lathered.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And the rider?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Farther away than when I started.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You never reached the ridge?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I reached every ridge I marked. The rider did not stay on them.

title: Before Brandon's Route
summary: The chronology matters: Raina saw the distance behavior before Samuel began planting identities and before she knew Brandon's route, preventing the Rider from being reduced to their manipulation campaign.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks Raina to pin the date against the Brannock timeline.
Raina uses her notebook to show Red Wash predates her first Brandon entry.
Samuel confirms he had not yet met Raina at that time.
Brandon notes that the earlier event may therefore have nothing to do with him at all.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: This was before the Last Drop?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Before I knew Brandon's name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Before I knew Raina.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then maybe the Rider has nothing to do with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That possibility matters.

title: Do Not Approach
summary: For once, Raina is the person arguing against pursuit. The group agrees to remain in camp, observe only, and let the Rider choose whether to approach.

panelPlan.text: The Rider remains on the rise as dusk deepens; no glow, impossible silhouette effect or visible motion.
Eva proposes taking optics closer from a shallow gully. Raina says not to.
Brandon points out the stranger has had ample opportunity to approach and has chosen not to.
Jessie assigns ordinary watches for safety without making the Rider the sole reason for them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We could get closer without riding at them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Do not pursue it tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You are the one telling me to stop?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I already ran that experiment with a horse under me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Let the stranger decide whether there is a conversation.

title: Night Watch
summary: The Rider remains a distant silhouette through part of the night, then becomes impossible to see in darkness. Nothing enters camp and no physical trace appears.

panelPlan.text: Blue-black night settles over the camp; the Rider's low rise becomes harder to separate from surrounding ground.
During Eva's watch, she can no longer tell whether the silhouette is present once the sky behind it darkens.
Brandon replaces her on watch and tells her to sleep rather than keep manufacturing certainty out of darkness.
The night passes without attack, sound, hoofbeats or unexplained light.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I can't tell whether they're still there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is becoming your favorite answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It is useful when it is true.

title: Empty Rise
summary: At first light, the low rise is empty. The ordinary relief lasts only until Jessie turns toward yesterday's road.

panelPlan.text: Dawn reveals the low rise clearly: no rider visible.
Eva uses optics and finds only rock and dry grass.
Brandon pours coffee while Raina checks the ground around camp for any sign of a night approach and finds none.
Jessie looks back along the road they traveled the previous day and stops packing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The rise is empty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then we can pack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Look behind us.

title: Behind Us
summary: A rider silhouette now stands on the road behind them, closer than the previous evening figure. The distance is small enough to be striking and still large enough to prevent identification.

panelPlan.text: Wide view back along the road: a mounted silhouette stands several hundred yards away where the road rises.
No tracks leading into camp are implied; the figure is simply present on the road.
Samuel compares the apparent distance to the previous evening's rise.
Raina has no explanation she trusts and does not pretend otherwise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: That is closer than last night.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you have an explanation?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Nothing I trust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Do you have one you don't trust?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Several. None improve with saying them aloud.

title: Coffee
summary: The issue closes without solving the Rider. Brandon insists on breakfast and continuing toward Saint Oren's, refusing to let unexplained observation become the only important fact in the world.

panelPlan.text: Eva, Jessie, Raina and Samuel remain focused on the Rider while Brandon pours coffee into dented cups.
He sets one cup in front of Eva without looking back at the road.
Jessie starts the rig. Nobody approaches the Rider and the Rider does not visibly approach them.
Final panel: the group resumes travel toward Saint Oren's while the unreadable silhouette remains behind at an honest distance with no supernatural effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You want coffee now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Especially now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Saint Oren's before noon if the road behaves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I am no longer using that phrase casually.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then drink before the language gets worse.

title: Next: FOUR QUIET DAYS
settingText: Saint Oren’s at dawn beneath an enormous dark structure. Ordinary smoke, breakfast activity and people beginning work; no anomaly, no rider, no portent. The tension comes from normality after the prior page.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 8. Point directly at the next loaded pressure without revealing its resolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They walked toward the Rider.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Distance did not behave.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They stopped chasing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Rider got closer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For the first time, Raina has no useful explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ahead, Saint Oren’s sits beneath an enormous Sunforge.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Eva has theories.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The town has its own business.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: FOUR QUIET DAYS
